summary: William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Harrow, Oxford, and Middle Temple, he studied under John Swinton, Mirza I'tisam-ud-Din, Ramachandra, and Ramalocana. He served as Chief Justice at Fort William and founded The Asiatic Society.

William L. Ames is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned degrees from Caltech and the University of Washington under supervisors David Seyfort Ruegg and Collett Cox, later holding posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

William M. Bodiford (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, among others. He taught at Meiji Gakuin, Davidson, and Iowa before joining UCLA around 1992.

William M. Gorvine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Connecticut College and the University of Virginia, he completed his Ph.D. under David F. Germano, having also studied under David Gordon White, Jeffrey Hopkins, and William Magee.

William Magee is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at the University of Virginia, Dharma Drum Institute, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert Buswell and earned his MA from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006.

William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College from around 1813 to 1830.

William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) was a religious studies and history scholar educated at Oxford and Yale. He held academic posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison before teaching at Harvard University from 1968.

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) was a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, holding professorial posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania.

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a linguist educated at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Denison, Baptist Union Seminary, and Yale, later serving as president of Bradley University and the University of Chicago.

William Roxburgh (1751–1815) was a scholar in Indology and botany. He studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Aberdeen/Marischal College. He served in the Madras Medical Service and directed Samalkot Garden and Calcutta Botanic Garden.

William S. Waldron is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1990 under Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita. He held posts at Otani University and Middlebury College.

William S.-Y. Wang (born 1933) is a linguistics and sinology scholar educated at Columbia and Michigan. He served on faculties including UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

William Stede (1882–1958) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He worked as an editor for the Pali Text Society (around 1916–1950) and held a teaching post at SOAS, University of London, between 1928 and 1949.

William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Attested in 2015, he founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and worked as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University.

William Ward (1769–1823) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ewood Hall Theological Academy under John Fawcett in 1797, served as a missionary at Serampore Mission (1800–1823), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1862–1887), as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886), and as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society.

William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Lycée Condorcet and École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr, later studying under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.

William Wright (1830–1889) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden, he served as Professor of Arabic at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, and Cambridge, and worked at the British Museum.

Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indology scholar who completed his Ph.D. under Hermann Jacobi and his habilitation at the University of Bonn. He worked at Bonn University and State Library and became a professor at Bonn in 1922.
